canonical.name: Mutual independence is inherited by subfamilies and remains true after complementing any selected events
canonical.source_note: No separately named heading occurs in the declared source blocks. This is the standard finite consequence of the mutual-independence product identities, proved by repeatedly expanding each complemented indicator as 1-I_A.

canonical.name: Product of arbitrary finite outcome-weight spaces and normalization of the product weights
canonical.source_note: Grinstead-Snell constructs the equal-factor case explicitly after Definition 4.5. The scaffold records the routine finite generalization to possibly different factors, with normalization proved by iterated finite sums.

canonical.name: Coordinate cylinder events are mutually independent under finite product probability
canonical.source_note: Grinstead-Snell identifies the coordinate random variables in its product construction as an independent-trials process. The scaffold states the corresponding cylinder-event theorem for arbitrary finite factors and proves it by factoring finite sums.

canonical.name: Events are independent if and only if their indicator random variables are independent
canonical.source_note: No selected source gives this equivalence its own heading. It follows in the finite setting by comparing the four joint atoms of (I_A,I_B) with the product of their Bernoulli marginals.

canonical.name: Finite second-moment lower bound P(X>0) >= E[X]^2/E[X^2] for nonnegative X
canonical.source_note: This is the direct finite Cauchy-Schwarz consequence obtained from X=X I_{X>0}; Pishro-Nik Section 6.2.4 supplies the cited Cauchy-Schwarz theorem and the scaffold records the one-line specialization.

canonical.name: Equality witness for Markov's inequality using X=a on an event of probability p and X=0 off that event
canonical.source_note: Pishro-Nik Section 6.2.2 states the nonnegative-variable hypothesis and the bound P(X>=a)<=E[X]/a for a>0. The canonical two-point witness has weights p and 1-p and realizes equality for every p in [0,1].

canonical.name: Counterexample showing that Markov's conclusion can fail without the nonnegativity hypothesis
canonical.source_note: Pishro-Nik Section 6.2.2 explicitly assumes that X is nonnegative. The canonical fair two-point witness X in {1,-3} has mean -1, while at threshold a=1 its upper-tail probability is 1/2, so the conclusion fails when that hypothesis is removed.
